This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.

2. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 01.01.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. petitioner was travelling in a Car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-P-5894 SCCH-5 along with his colleagues on Bengaluru - Mysuru Road, near Basava Gayhathri Ashrama, Kumbalagodu, Kengeri Hobli,
Bengaluru, which was being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the centre divider and then dashed against center flyover pillar, as a result of this car was moved reverse and dashed against left side grill of wall.
Due to the said impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
he was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical College Hospital, after first-aid he was shifted to Supra Hospital and took treatment as inpatient.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 37 years, hale and healthy, working as Loan Recovery Agent and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to the accidental injuries, and subsisting disability, the SCCH-5 petitioner has lost the prospectus of good health, better employment etc.,
With regard to accident crime No.01/2023 is registered against the driver of the said car before the Kumbalagodu P.S. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer

,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement.

In the written statement respondent No.1 denied occurrence of the alleged accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle, injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by him,
expenses incurred towards treatment.

Further submitted that, the Car bearing Reg.

2 v i d e p o l i c y No.98000031210111216046 valid from 24.02.2022 to 23.02.2023, which is valid as on the date of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-P-5894 drove the same without having a valid and specific endorsement driving license, which is in contravention of the policy.
Further submitted that, that said vehicle was insured vide policy No.98000031210111216046 valid from 24.02.2022 to midnight of 23.02.2023.

Further submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioner SCCH-5 is highly excessive, arbitrary.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::

1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-P-5894 by its driver, in RTA took place on 01.01.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. on Bengaluru - Mysuru Road, near Basavagangothri Ashrama, Kumbalagodu, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru City?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, wife/next friend of the petitioner is examined as PW-1, examined Dr.Srihari SCCH-5 B.G., Consultant Neurosurgeon at Supra Hospital is examined as PW-2,
Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics as PW-3 and marked 20 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR and complaint as Ex.P.1, copy of spot mahazar along with sketch as Ex.P.2, copy of Sec.133 notice and reply as Ex.P.3, copy of wound certificate as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.5.
11.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Doctors as PW-2 and PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 corroborates the SCCH-5 case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 01.01.2023 as alleged in the petition.
12. Further examined PI, APTS, Yelanaka as RW-1 and marked copy of charge sheet as Ex.R.1.
During the cross examination of R.W-1 it is elicited that as accused fled away from the spot the medical examination regarding consumption of alcohol is not done.
As per R.W-1 he collected CCTV footage regarding consumption of alcohol by the accused but said evidence is not produced before this court.
As per version of R.W-1 except filing chargesheet regarding drunken driving no cogent evidence is produced by the respondent No.1.
Thus negligence cannot be attributed to respondent No.1.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 01.01.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. SCCH-5 when he was traveling in a Car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-P- 5894 on Bengaluru-Mysuru Road, near Basava Gayathri Ashrama,
Kumbalagodu, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru.
13. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-P-5894.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the PW-1, petitioner had sustained severe head injury,
contusion of right temporal lobe, fracture of left FTP greater wing of sphenoid bone, S/P right decompressive craniotomy with clot evacuation S/P tracheostomy, cervical vertibra C7 fracture, C6 spinous process fracture, cord contusion of SCCH-5 C6 level, compression fracture of superior end plate of C3 vertibra, fracture of bilateral transverse process of L3 vertibra, fracture of right transverse process of L4 vertibra, fracture of right lamina and pedicle L3.
For the said injuries petitioner underwent multiple operations.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.4, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.6 issued by Supra Hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 01.01.2023 to 25.01.2023, from 24.02.2023 to 25.02.2023, thereafter from 28.03.2023 to 30.03.2023, 21.04.2023 to 23.04.2023, 10.05.2023 to 15.05.2023.
Further PW-1 has exhibited medical prescriptions as Ex.P.11 and medical bills of Rs.15,10,392/- as Ex.P.12.

15. Further Dr.Srihari B.G. Consultant Neurosurgeon in Supra Hospital is examined as PW-2 SCCH-5 and got marked OPD Sheet as Ex.P.13, neuro psychological assessment as Ex.P.14, case sheet as Ex.P.15, MRI Brain Film with reports as Ex.P.16. PW-2
has assessed whole body permanent disability of 35%.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he is not treated Doctor and he is Neuro Surgeon.
Further deposed that, in head injury if the blood gets clot, then the injuries mentioned in his reports does not happens and the wound may heal early in the youngsters.

Further Manjunatha H.S vs Naveen V on 31 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121183990/

16. PW-1 has also examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics as PW-3, who got marked MRI report as Ex.P.17, X-ray Films as Ex.P.18,
MRI-Scan as Ex.P.19 and clinical notes as Ex.P.20.

sentences.text: PW-3 has assessed permanent physical disability in relation to spine to whole body is 15%.

During the course of cross- examination PW-3 deposed that, he is not treated Doctor and on 18.01.2025 petitioner has approached him along with one assistant and could walk independently only with support of his assistant.
Further deposed that, he has assessed only spine disability and there is fracture in L3 and L4 bone and fractures are united.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries SCCH-5 sustained by the petitioner the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 15% for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

17. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 37 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.9, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.06.1985 and the alleged accident is occurred on 01.01.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.9 his age is considered about 38 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 35 days.

As per the evidence of PW-3 he has examined petitioner on 18.01.2025 i.e., after 2 years of the accident and as per version of PW-2, PW-3 and by SCCH-5 considering the gravity of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least three months to heal the wound.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income.
As per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.16,000/- p.m.

20. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.12 medical bills for Rs.15,10,392/-.
On perusal of the said bills, it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.4 in which Doctor who have treated has SCCH-5 categorically stated that,
petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 01.01.2023.

So as per Ex.P.4 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained head injury acute SAH/SDH, C6, C7 cervical vertebrae fracture, fracture bilateral transverse process of L3 vertebrae and L4 vertebrae with right lamina and pedicle, which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Naveen V. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A), 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
21.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
SCCH-5 Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 4,32,000-00
2. Pain and sufferings 25,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 15,10,392-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 48,000 -00 period

Accordingly this tribunal hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.
20,45,392/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
23.
The respondent No.2 contended that the driver of car was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident hence respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation.

In this regard counsel for Respondent No.2 relied on decision reported in IFFCO TOKIO SCCH-5 GENERAL INSURANCE LTD v/s PEARL BEVERAGES LTD wherein Hon'ble Apex court set aside the orders of NCDRC and absolved liability of insurance company by holding that the driver of car was under the influence of alcohol.

The respondent No.2 in the case on hand not proved through the evidence of R.W-2 that the driver of car was under the influence of alcohol.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has Manjunatha H.S vs Naveen V on 31 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121183990/
6 issued insurance policy bearing No.9800003121011 1216046 which is valid for the period from 24.02.2022 to 23.02.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 01.01.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

sentences.text: Therefore the liability of SCCH-5 respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

24. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,45,392/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs Forty Five Thousand Three Hundred Ninety Two Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details SCCH-5 along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
